title: A list of bytes crosses the guest boundary as one wasmtime `Val` per byte.
text: `convert` lowers `Value::Bytes` to a `Val::List` of `Val::U8` and lifts it back the same way, because the call bridge calls every export through wasmtime's dynamic `Func::call_async`. Each byte costs a whole `Val` on the host, so a crossing costs tens of nanoseconds per byte; `benches/results/image-guest.json` shows returning decoded pixels costing about ten times the decode. Both directions are charged to the request: the hostcall fuel bounds a lift, the lifted results are charged while they are converted, and the lowered arguments are charged until the guest returns (`crates/nvs-ext/src/call.rs`'s `Request::run`). The decided fix is wasmtime's typed calls for exports whose parameters or results are `list<u8>`. A typed call needs a Rust type for every parameter and result, and wasmtime fixes each type's layout at compile time (`ComponentType::ABI`, a `const`), so a type built from the manifest at run time cannot be one. The exports that move the most bytes, such as `image`'s `run(source, plan)`, carry their bytes inside records and variants. Covering them needs a choice from the user: Rust bindings generated for each first-party world, with a conversion from `Value` per world; a typed path only for exports whose whole signature is scalars, strings, `list<u8>` and the world's `error`, which leaves `run` dynamic; or a change to the first-party worlds that moves the bytes to a top-level parameter or a lent `value`. `crates/nvs-ext/tests/support/image_arms.rs` sizes its frame for the per-byte cost until then.
